origin.description: Extract words start through end. A negative index counts back from the last word.
origin.usage: word(string, start = 1L, end = start, sep = fixed(" "))

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: start
arguments.text: First word to keep, counting from 1. A negative value counts from the last word. The default is 1.

arguments.name: end
arguments.text: Last word to keep, inclusive. It defaults to start. A negative value counts from the last word.

arguments.name: sep
arguments.text: Separator between words. The default is a single space, matched as fixed text.

origin.details: The separator is located, then the gaps between matches are the words. An index of 0 is a missing word. An index past the last word is missing. string, start, and end are recycled together.
origin.value: A character vector the same length as string, start, and end.
origin.example:
sentences <- c("Jane saw a cat", "Jane sat down")
print(word(sentences, 1))
print(word(sentences, 2))
print(word(sentences, -1))
print(word(sentences, 2, -1))
print(word(sentences[1], 1:3, -1))
print(word(sentences[1], 1, 1:4))
str <- "abc.def..123.4568.999"
print(word(str, 1, sep = fixed("..")))
print(word(str, 2, sep = fixed("..")))

translation.description: Extract words start through end. A negative index counts back from the last word. The result is a list. A missing string is stringi._na.NA.

translation.details: The separator is located, then the gaps between matches are the words. An index of 0 is a missing word. An index past the last word is missing. string, start, and end are recycled together. The Python result is a list, and a missing string is stringi._na.NA.
translation.value: A character vector the same length as string, start, and end.
translation.example:
from stringr.pattern import fixed
from stringr.word import word
sentences = ["Jane saw a cat", "Jane sat down"]
print(word(sentences, 1))
print(word(sentences, 2))
print(word(sentences, -1))
print(word(sentences, 2, -1))
print(word(sentences[0], [1, 2, 3], -1))
print(word(sentences[0], 1, [1, 2, 3, 4]))
text = "abc.def..123.4568.999"
print(word(text, 1, sep=fixed("..")))
print(word(text, 2, sep=fixed("..")))
